title: NumPy — from essentials to applications
description: A progressive hands-on track covering arrays, vectorization, broadcasting, statistics, linear algebra, and practical numerical-analysis patterns.

numpy-foundations-001.title: Your first ndarray
numpy-foundations-001.objective: Create arrays and inspect their structure.
numpy-foundations-001.description: Create the `notas` vector with 7.5, 8.0, 9.5, and 6.0. Display the array, number of dimensions, shape, and element count.
requirements: Use np.array with a floating-point dtype
numpy-foundations-001.hint: Array metadata is exposed as attributes, not methods.

numpy-foundations-002.title: Sequences without typing
numpy-foundations-002.objective: Generate regular sequences with the right tool.
numpy-foundations-002.description: Create `pares` from 2 through 20 with step 2, and `pontos` with five evenly spaced values from 0 to 1, including both endpoints.
requirements: Do not type the values manually
numpy-foundations-002.hint: arange prioritizes the step; linspace prioritizes the count.

numpy-foundations-003.title: Ready-made matrices
numpy-foundations-003.description: Create `zeros` with shape 2x3, `preenchida` with shape 2x2 filled with 7, and a 3x3 `identidade` matrix.
numpy-foundations-003.hint: Pass the shape as a tuple for multidimensional arrays.

numpy-foundations-004.title: Types under control
numpy-foundations-004.description: Convert `valores` into 32-bit `inteiros` and 64-bit `precisos` without changing the original array.

numpy-shape-001.title: Array X-ray
numpy-shape-001.objective: Relate shape, type, and memory use.
numpy-shape-001.description: Build `dados` as a 3x4 matrix of 16-bit integers and create the `info` dictionary with shape, dtype as text, itemsize, and nbytes.
numpy-shape-001.hint: nbytes equals size multiplied by itemsize.

numpy-shape-002.title: Reshape without losing data
numpy-shape-002.objective: Change shape while keeping data order.
numpy-shape-002.description: Turn `sequencia` into a three-row `matriz`, letting NumPy infer the number of columns.
numpy-shape-002.hint: The total element count must stay the same.

numpy-shape-003.title: View or copy?
numpy-shape-003.description: From `matriz`, create `vista` with ravel and `copia` with flatten. Set the first item in `vista` to 99 and observe which object follows the change.

numpy-shape-004.title: Axes in motion
numpy-shape-004.description: Create `transposta` by swapping rows and columns in `matriz`, and `trocado` by swapping the first two axes in `cubo`.
numpy-shape-004.hint: swapaxes takes the indexes of the two axes.

numpy-shape-005.title: Dimensions on demand
numpy-shape-005.description: Turn `vetor` into `coluna` with shape (4,1), then recover `restaurado` with shape (4,).
numpy-shape-005.hint: np.newaxis is an alias for None used in indexing.

numpy-indexing-001.title: Slices are views
numpy-indexing-001.objective: Use slicing and recognize shared memory.
numpy-indexing-001.description: Extract the central 2x2 block of `grade` into `centro`. Multiply that block by -1 in-place and confirm the grid changes.
numpy-indexing-001.hint: The central block occupies rows and columns 1:3.

numpy-indexing-002.title: Out-of-order selection
numpy-indexing-002.objective: Select arbitrary positions with index arrays.
numpy-indexing-002.description: Create `selecionados` from positions 4, 1, and 5 of `valores`, in that order. Then change selecionados and verify valores does not change.
requirements: Use a list or array of indexes
Recognize that the result is a copy

numpy-indexing-003.title: Vectorized filter
numpy-indexing-003.description: Select grades at least 7 into `aprovados` and grades from 5 up to, but not including, 7 into `recuperacao`.
requirements: Do not use a list comprehension

numpy-indexing-004.title: Element-wise choice
numpy-indexing-004.description: Clamp `temperaturas` to the 0..40 range in `ajustadas`, and create `rotulos` with 'alta' for original values above 30 and 'ok' otherwise.

numpy-indexing-005.title: Multiple conditions
numpy-indexing-005.objective: Classify values using several vectorized rules.
numpy-indexing-005.description: Classify `idades` as criança (<12), adolescente (<18), adulto (<60), or idoso otherwise, saving the result in `faixas`.
numpy-indexing-005.hint: np.select takes a list of conditions and a list of choices.

numpy-broadcasting-001.title: Row plus column
numpy-broadcasting-001.objective: Combine compatible shapes without manual replication.
numpy-broadcasting-001.description: Add `linha` with shape (3,) to `coluna` with shape (2,1), saving the 2x3 matrix in `somas`.
requirements: Do not use tile or loops
numpy-broadcasting-001.hint: Dimensions are compared from right to left.

numpy-broadcasting-002.title: Column normalization
numpy-broadcasting-002.objective: Center columns using reduction and broadcasting.
numpy-broadcasting-002.description: Create `centralizada` by subtracting each column's own mean from `dados`. Keep the means' dimension in `medias`.
numpy-broadcasting-002.hint: keepdims yields shape (1,3), compatible with the matrix.

numpy-ufuncs-001.title: Ufunc with a selective destination
numpy-ufuncs-001.objective: Control where and into which buffer a ufunc writes.
numpy-ufuncs-001.description: In `raizes`, calculate square roots only for non-negative values. Keep -1 in all other positions by using the out and where parameters of np.sqrt.
numpy-ufuncs-001.hint: The where parameter does not automatically fill false positions.

numpy-aggregation-001.title: Reduce along the right axis
numpy-aggregation-001.objective: Interpret reductions by row and column.
numpy-aggregation-001.description: Calculate `somas_colunas`, `maximos_linhas`, and the `total` of the dados matrix.
numpy-aggregation-001.hint: Removing axis 0 aggregates rows and leaves one output per column.

numpy-aggregation-002.title: Where is the extreme?
numpy-aggregation-002.description: Find the column of each row's maximum in `colunas_max`, and the (row,column) position of the global minimum in `posicao_min`.
requirements: Convert the flat index with unravel_index

numpy-aggregation-003.title: Missing data
numpy-aggregation-003.description: Calculate column means ignoring NaN in `medias`, and create `limpo` by replacing each NaN with its column mean.
requirements: Use broadcasting or indexing to fill values
numpy-aggregation-003.hint: np.where with np.isnan can combine dados and medias.

numpy-combine-001.title: Join or stack
numpy-combine-001.objective: Choose between extending an axis and creating a new one.
numpy-combine-001.description: Join a and b into `concatenado` with shape (6,), and stack both into `empilhado` with shape (2,3).
numpy-combine-001.hint: stack creates a new axis; concatenate uses an existing one.

numpy-combine-002.title: Balanced splitting
numpy-combine-002.objective: Partition arrays and understand uneven divisions.
numpy-combine-002.description: Split `dados` into three equal parts in `iguais`, and into four possible parts in `flexiveis`.

numpy-combine-003.title: Repeat with intent
numpy-combine-003.objective: Distinguish repeating elements from repeating patterns.
numpy-combine-003.description: Create `repetido` by repeating each base item twice, and `mosaico` by repeating the complete pattern three times.
numpy-combine-003.hint: repeat acts on elements; tile acts on the block.

numpy-order-001.title: Sort while preserving the source
numpy-order-001.objective: Sort values and carry associated indexes.
numpy-order-001.description: Calculate `ordem` that sorts pontuacoes in ascending order, then use it to create `nomes_ordenados` without changing the original arrays.
numpy-order-001.hint: argsort returns the indexes that would sort an array.

numpy-order-002.title: Values and frequencies
numpy-order-002.description: Extract sorted unique categories into `valores` and their frequencies into `contagens`.

numpy-order-003.title: Efficient integer counting
numpy-order-003.objective: Count non-negative integers and bin measurements.
numpy-order-003.description: Create `frequencias` for integer grades 0..5 with bincount, and `histograma` for bins [0,3) and [3,6].
requirements: Also save the edges in bordas
numpy-order-003.hint: bincount uses each value itself as an index.

numpy-order-004.title: Coordinates that matter
numpy-order-004.objective: Locate elements that satisfy a condition.
numpy-order-004.description: Find coordinates (row,column) of values above 5 in `posicoes`, and separate indexes in `linhas` and `colunas`.
numpy-order-004.hint: argwhere stacks coordinates; nonzero returns one tuple item per axis.

numpy-linalg-001.title: The right product for each case
numpy-linalg-001.description: Calculate `produto_escalar` between u and v, and `produto_matricial` between A and B using the @ operator.
numpy-linalg-001.hint: The left column count must match the right row count.

numpy-linalg-002.title: Solve without inverting
numpy-linalg-002.description: Solve Ax=b in `solucao` with np.linalg.solve and confirm in `residuo` that A @ solucao - b is near zero.
numpy-linalg-002.hint: A direct solve is more stable and efficient than inv(A) @ b.

numpy-linalg-003.title: Distances by norm
numpy-linalg-003.objective: Calculate norms for several observations at once.
numpy-linalg-003.description: In `normas`, calculate the Euclidean norm of each row in pontos; in `distancias`, calculate each point's distance to referencia.

numpy-random-001.title: Reproducible randomness
numpy-random-001.objective: Generate reproducible samples with the modern API.
numpy-random-001.description: Create `rng` with seed 42 and generate a 2x3 `amostra` matrix of integers from 1 through 9.
numpy-random-001.hint: The upper bound of integers is exclusive.

numpy-random-002.title: Distribution at scale
numpy-random-002.objective: Sample a distribution and summarize the result.
numpy-random-002.description: With an rng seeded at 7, generate `dados` containing 10,000 normal values with mean 100 and standard deviation 15. Calculate `media` and `desvio`.
numpy-random-002.hint: Large samples approximate the parameters but are not identical to them.

numpy-random-003.title: Sample without replacement
numpy-random-003.objective: Sample and shuffle without changing the source.
numpy-random-003.description: With seed 21, choose three distinct names without replacement in `sorteio`, and create `embaralhado` as a permutation of all names.
numpy-random-003.example_output:
three distinct names
all five names in a new order
numpy-random-003.hint: Use the same generator for both operations to get a deterministic sequence.

numpy-io-001.title: Binary array bundle
numpy-io-001.objective: Persist multiple arrays while preserving types and shapes.
numpy-io-001.description: Save a and b to `dados.npz` with explicit names, load the file, and copy its arrays to `carregado_a` and `carregado_b`.
requirements: Access the a and b keys
numpy-io-001.hint: Use a with block when opening the NpzFile.

numpy-io-002.title: Interoperable text
numpy-io-002.objective: Exchange numerical matrices in text form.
numpy-io-002.description: Save dados to `dados.csv` using commas and two decimal places; load it back into `carregado`.
numpy-io-002.hint: Use the same delimiter when reading.

numpy-vectorization-001.title: Conversion without a loop
numpy-vectorization-001.objective: Replace Python iteration with bulk calculation.
numpy-vectorization-001.description: Convert every Celsius temperature to Fahrenheit in `fahrenheit` with a single vectorized expression.
requirements: Do not use for or a comprehension
numpy-vectorization-001.hint: Arithmetic operators are applied element by element.

numpy-vectorization-002.title: All distances at once
numpy-vectorization-002.objective: Calculate a distance matrix without loops.
numpy-vectorization-002.description: In `distancias`, calculate all Euclidean distances between every row of A and every row of B. The output must have shape (3,2).
requirements: Use norm on the last axis

numpy-grids-001.title: Function over a grid
numpy-grids-001.description: Create X and Y with meshgrid from x=[-1,0,1] and y=[-2,0,2], then calculate `Z = X**2 + Y**2`.
numpy-grids-001.hint: With default indexing, every row of X repeats x.

numpy-advanced-001.title: Einstein in one line
numpy-advanced-001.objective: Express products and traces through indexes.
numpy-advanced-001.description: Use np.einsum to calculate the matrix `produto` of A and B, and `diagonal` containing A's diagonal elements.
numpy-advanced-001.hint: Repeated letters indicate contracted axes or diagonals.

numpy-advanced-002.title: Sliding windows
numpy-advanced-002.objective: Create overlapping windows without manual copies.
numpy-advanced-002.description: Create size-three `janelas` over serie and calculate `media_movel` for each window.

numpy-applied-001.title: One-hot encoding
numpy-applied-001.description: Convert rotulos into a `one_hot` matrix with four rows and three classes using NumPy indexing.

numpy-applied-002.title: Robust standardization
numpy-applied-002.description: Standardize each column of X into `padronizado` using population mean and standard deviation. Protect constant columns by replacing zero deviation with 1 in `escala`.
requirements: Calculate mean and std by column
Use np.where for a safe scale
Do not produce NaN or infinity
numpy-applied-002.example_output:
columns have mean 0
variable columns have deviation 1
numpy-applied-002.hint: A constant column must become zeros.

numpy-applied-003.title: Confusion matrix
numpy-applied-003.objective: Accumulate class pairs in a vectorized way.
numpy-applied-003.description: Build a 3x3 `matriz_confusao` where rows are true classes and columns are predicted classes, accumulating every pair.
numpy-applied-003.hint: np.add.at(matriz, (reais, previstas), 1) handles repeated indexes correctly.

numpy-applied-004.title: Mini-batches
numpy-applied-004.description: With seed 5, create `indices` as a permutation of X's eight rows, produce `embaralhado = X[indices]`, and reshape into `lotes` with shape (4,2,2).
numpy-applied-004.hint: Four batches, two samples per batch, two features per sample.

numpy-applied-005.title: Sensor pipeline
numpy-applied-005.objective: Combine NumPy techniques in a realistic flow.
numpy-applied-005.description: In `limpo`, replace NaN with each column's median and clamp values to [0,100]. Then calculate `resumo` containing each column's mean for groups 0 and 1, producing shape (2,3).
numpy-applied-005.hint: One vectorized group solution is to stack means calculated through masks.
